_about: Terrain parameters for Track T (scripts/world/terrain.gd generates from them, scripts/render/terrain_draw.gd and terrain_shadows.gd draw from them). EVERY VALUE IS PROPOSED by Track T on 2026-10-09: the design doc leaves the form of height, how height reads in ink, map size and pixels per world unit open (Open design details: Camera and scale, World generation, Terrain and biomes). Record shape as in data/sim/turn.json: {value, _proposed, _reason} until a decision in data/decisions/decisions.json replaces _proposed with its id. World units are METRES; drawing converts with scale.px_per_m. Tree sizes, collision radii, line weights, ink, paper and the sun stay in data/params/render_defaults.json (read through RenderParams); this file only adds what terrain needs.

px_per_m._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 accepted this as the demo baseline. Was proposed: PLACEHOLDER, NOT A PICK (the scale is Alex's open question; the report gives three options with their arithmetic). 4 px/m is option A, true scale at the prototype's tree scale: the prototype's 38 px canopy is then a 9.5 m crown, a mature broadleaf, and a 256 m chunk is a 1024 px texture

bounds_source._reason: Track S owns the map size (exit criterion 5 is a flight rule; its _derivation sizes the map from the planes' envelopes). Terrain reads map_bounds_m.value from that file so the two can never disagree

fallback_bounds_m._reason: used only when bounds_source is missing or has no map_bounds_m; the same 5000 m square Track S proposed

chunk_m._reason: a chunk is generated from (seed, chunk x, chunk y) alone; 256 m is 1024 px at 4 px/m, one power-of-two texture for Track V's baked map view, and a 5000 m map is 20 x 20 chunks

cell_m._reason: marching-squares grid: 32 x 32 cells a chunk. Fine enough for the smallest octave of the height noise (about 30 m), coarse enough that a chunk's field is 1089 noise samples

noise_per_m._reason: fbm lattice every 250 m: plateaus a few hundred metres across, so a 320 x 180 m view at zoom 1 often has a scarp in it and a 5 km map has a few dozen uplands

octaves._reason: down to a ~30 m lattice: ragged enough edges for bays and spurs, no detail finer than the 8 m grid resolves

seed_offset._reason: height noise seed = scene seed % 9973 + 101, the prototype's own way of deriving a field seed (its grove field is seed % 9973 + 3), so the height and grove fields are independent

thresholds._reason: fbm >= 0.56 is upland (level 1), >= 0.66 is the high top (level 2). Two thresholds give the required two levels plus a cheap third; about a third of the map is upland and a tenth of that is high ground

level_heights_m._reason: one level per threshold plus the low ground. 12 m is a clear escarpment that casts a shadow about twice a tree's (46 px against ~24 px at 46 degrees, 4 px/m); 24 m for the top. Track S's constraint holds: 24 m plus the tallest tree (~14 m) stays under the 120 m low air band

chaikin_passes._reason: as the prototype smooths a freehand wall: two passes turn the marching-squares polyline into a hand-drawn curve

resample_m._reason: 4 px between contour points at 4 px/m, close to the prototype's 3 px road and wall sampling

width_m._reason: the scarp is drawn as a band on the low side of the level boundary (the boundary is its top edge); 5 m (20 px) holds a row of hachures without eating the low ground

dart_area_px._reason: the prototype's dart count, W*H/75 darts per stage, per chunk

density_noise_per_px._reason: the prototype's grove field, fbm(x*.006, y*.006, ...), in world pixels so groves run on across chunk borders

levels._reason: one entry per level, the prototype's rule `f < threshold || rng() > (f - threshold) * gain` with its own .5 and 3.2 on the low ground; the upland a little sparser and the top sparser again, so the levels differ in texture as well as tone

clearance_below_cr._reason: a tree on the low side of a scarp keeps its trunk off the slope: its centre stays scarp width + 0.5 x its collision radius from the boundary, so the hachures read

clearance_above_cr._reason: a tree on top may stand at the edge with its canopy overhanging the slope, as trees on a bluff do; only its trunk keeps a quarter of its collision radius back

style._reason: Alex 2026-10-09 strongly prefers contours visually (variants/height-in-ink/). What the line breaks should signal is still open; hachures stay available as the other value. Was proposed: FIRST OPTION for the open question 'how height reads in ink (contours, hachures or shading)': one contour at the scarp top plus hachures down the slope. 'contours' draws two or three nested contours instead, so a board can show both

ok_lightness_step._reason: each level's paper is the paper lifted by one fill-ramp step in OK lightness (palette proposal: lightness is a ramp off paper, never a new hue). 0.025 is under the wall fill's +0.033, so level 2 (+0.05) still sits below the trees' object fill (+0.078)

chroma_scale_per_step._reason: chroma eased as the fill lightens, as the prototype's fills do (paper C 0.048 to wall fill 0.040)

weight._reason: a line-weight multiplier NAMED from render_defaults.json linework, so terrain shares the one weight table: a scarp top is an earthwork edge, 1.15 x

alpha._reason: nearly full ink, like the tree rings' .88

wobble._reason: fraction of the prototype's road-rut wobble, (noise - .5) * 2.6 * (.35 + hand wobble): about +/- 0.6 px at the default hand wobble

wobble_noise_per_px._reason: the rut wobble's frequency (.09 per 3 px sample)

spacing_px._reason: dense enough to read as a tone band at zoom 1, open enough that single strokes still show

long._reason: long strokes run the full scarp width

short._reason: alternating long and short strokes, the cartographer's escarpment sign

length_jitter._reason: noise-driven length spread, so the foot of the scarp is ragged rather than ruled

angle_jitter._reason: radians of noise-driven lean, a hand's inconsistency

weight._reason: named linework multiplier: the prototype's lightest ground line, 0.8 x

alpha._reason: lighter than the contour so the edge reads first

shape._reason: 'wedge' tapers each stroke from the top (a filled sliver, the design doc's wanted tapered stroke); 'stroke' is a plain hairline

wedge_width_px._reason: base width of a wedge; it tapers to 15% of this at the foot

break_noise_per_px._reason: the prototype's broken-line noise frequency (rut lines, .045 per 3 px sample)

break_threshold._reason: skip a stroke where that noise is under .25 (the ruts use .3), so the band has gaps like a pen lifting

count._reason: the alternative style: the scarp top plus two lines down the slope

spacing_scarp._reason: lines every half scarp width, so the last one is the scarp foot

break_thresholds._reason: the top line is unbroken, the lower ones break like the wall crest lines

break_noise_per_px._reason: the same broken-line frequency as the hachures (the prototype's rut lines)

weight._reason: named linework multiplier for the lines below the top one

lee_dot_min._reason: a boundary segment casts a prism only when its down-slope normal faces at most this far toward the sun; sun-facing segments would only sweep over the upland itself, which the receiver cut removes anyway
